entities.summary:
Diogenes Laërtius (c. 200 BCE) was a Greek biographer and philosopher who remains a crucial figure in understanding ancient Greek philosophy.

As the primary source for the history of Greek philosophy, his work, Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, is still studied and referenced today.

Born in Athens, Greece, Diogenes Laërtius was educated in Athens and later traveled extensively throughout the Mediterranean, collecting information and anecdotes about famous philosophers and their teachings.

His reputation is complex, with some scholars praising his dedication to preserving the works of ancient Greek philosophers, while others criticize his lack of critical evaluation and his focus on trivial details.

Despite these criticisms, Diogenes Laërtius's work continues to be an essential resource for historians and scholars of ancient Greek philosophy.

entities.summary:
Diogenes Laërtius was a biographer and philosopher of the Hellenistic period, best known for his Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers, a comprehensive collection of biographical sketches and philosophical treatises on some of the most influential figures of ancient Greek philosophy. His work, which was widely read and respected in the ancient world, provides valuable insights into the lives and ideas of prominent philosophers such as Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle. Despite its enduring influence, Diogenes Laërtius' own life and intentions remain shrouded in mystery, with many scholars questioning the accuracy and reliability of his accounts.

Diogenes Laërtius was born in Athens, Greece, around 200 BCE and lived in the 2nd century BCE. He is thought to have been a student of the philosopher Philodemus and to have traveled extensively throughout the ancient Mediterranean world, gathering material for his biographical work. His work was widely disseminated and admired in the ancient world, with many of his sources, including the philosopher Plutarch, drawing heavily on his accounts.

Diogenes Laërtius' legacy extends far beyond his own work, influencing the development of Western philosophy and the study of ancient Greek thought. His Lives and Opinions of Eminent Philosophers remains a fundamental source for the history of philosophy, and his approach to biography and philosophy continues to shape the field to this day.

The impact of Diogenes Laërtius' work can be seen in the many subsequent biographies and histories of ancient Greek philosophers, as well as in the ongoing debate among scholars about the accuracy and reliability of his accounts. His work continues to be widely read and studied, offering a unique window into the lives and ideas of some of the most influential figures in Western philosophical history.
